extracted.intended_audience: psychologists, researchers, and clinicians interested in measuring individual differences in humor styles
extracted.subtask_description: Using the Humor Styles Questionnaire (HSQ) to measure four distinct ways individuals use humor: self-enhancing, affiliative, aggressive, and self-defeating. The HSQ is a self-report instrument designed to capture both benign and potentially detrimental uses of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-enhancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Relatively benign uses of humor to enhance the self (Self-enhancing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses a person's tendency to use humor in ways that maintain or enhance their own outlook and psychological well-being; characterized as a benign, adaptive humor style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliative
rubrics_metrics.description: Relatively benign uses of humor to enhance one's relationships with others (Affiliative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures use of humor to facilitate social interaction, reduce tensions, and build relationships; considered an adaptive, relationship-enhancing style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggressive
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of humor to enhance the self at the expense of others (Aggressive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures hostile, disparaging, or hurtful humor directed at others; identified as a less desirable style that can be detrimental to interpersonal relationships and others' well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-defeating
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of humor to enhance relationships at the expense of self (Self-defeating).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses self-disparaging or self-subordinating humor used to ingratiate oneself or gain social approval; regarded as potentially harmful to the individual's psychological well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement approach: self-report HSQ
rubrics_metrics.description: The Humor Styles Questionnaire is a self-report measure that assesses four dimensions of humor use, including ways that are less desirable and potentially detrimental (Aggressive and Self-defeating).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The HSQ represents a novel measurement approach by explicitly including maladaptive humor styles; intended for use in research/clinical settings to index individual differences in how humor is used.
